claim_verdicts.evidence: OpenTelemetry primer: "Observability lets you understand a system from the outside by letting you ask questions about that system without knowing its inner workings. Furthermore, it allows you to easily troubleshoot and handle novel problems, that is, \"unknown unknowns\"." Round 2: the monitoring half is now scoped 'as the dashboard lessons use it'; those panels are fixed queries provisioned in donhang-api.json @ stage-2 (see claim 3), i.e. answers decided in advance.

stage-2 docker-compose.yml api env: Logging__Console__FormatterName: "json"; Program.cs: app.UseHttpMetrics(), app.MapMetrics(); Directory.Packages.props @ stage-2 contains prometheus-net.AspNetCore 8.2.1 and no OpenTelemetry package (grep returned only the prometheus-net line).

donhang-api.json @ stage-2 line 64 "title": "5xx responses per second", line 100 "expr": "sum(rate(http_requests_received_total{code=~\"5..\"}[5m]))" — one summed rate, no per-request or per-order label.

Docs: "The order you add middleware components in the Program.cs file defines the order in which the middleware components are invoked on requests and the reverse order for the response." Program.cs @ stage-2: app.UseMiddleware<RequestLoggingMiddleware>(); then app.UseMiddleware<ExceptionHandlingMiddleware>(); RequestLoggingMiddleware logs after `await next(context)`, ExceptionHandlingMiddleware logs inside its catch before WriteProblemAsync.

Captured stage-2 line: {"EventId":0,"LogLevel":"Information","Category":"DonHang.Api.Middleware.RequestLoggingMiddleware","Message":"GET /api/v1/products/2 responded 200 in ...ms","State":{"Method":...,"Path":...,"StatusCode":200,"ElapsedMs":...}}. Docs: "When an ILogger object is created, a category is specified... the convention is to use the fully qualified class name." Both middleware take ILogger<T> of their own class.

Execution: stage-2 captured request line (written inside the request, where hosting opens a scope) has no Scopes key. Compose @ stage-2 sets only FormatterName (IncludeScopes appears only from stage-3); appsettings.json sets none. Scratch net10.0 app with only FormatterName=json, LogError inside a request: line ends "State":{"{OriginalFormat}":"unhandled exception"}} — no Scopes. API doc for IncludeScopes states no default.

Code: ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.cs @ stage-2 last catch: `logger.LogError(ex, "unhandled exception"); await WriteProblemAsync(context, StatusCodes.Status500InternalServerError, ...)`. Execution (scratch net10.0, JSON formatter, same call): {"EventId":0,"LogLevel":"Error","Category":"Demo.ExceptionHandlingMiddleware","Message":"unhandled exception","Exception":"System.InvalidOperationException: ... at ...","State":{"{OriginalFormat}":"unhandled exception"}}. Exception text present; no method/path field.
claim_verdicts.source: DonHang.Api/Middleware/ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.cs @ stage-2; scratch run of LogError(ex, msg) with Logging:Console:FormatterName=json

claim_verdicts.evidence: Captured: "== POST /api/v1/orders for a product that does not exist\n  -> 500" then {"LogLevel":"Information","Category":"DonHang.Api.Middleware.RequestLoggingMiddleware","Message":"POST /api/v1/orders responded 500 in ...ms"}. OrderService.PlaceOrderAsync @ stage-2 does no product lookup before SaveChangesAsync; FK 23503 is not UniqueViolation, so the generic catch answers 500.

NotificationSender.cs @ stage-2: `private static readonly TimeSpan Tick = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2);`, `while (await timer.WaitForNextTickAsync(stoppingToken))`, and in SendOneAsync after email.SendAsync: `logger.LogInformation("Sent notification {NotificationId} for order {OrderId}", notification.Id, notification.OrderId);`

Loki 3.5 log queries: "Adding | json to your pipeline will extract all json properties as labels if the log line is a valid json document."; string label filters: "you can use the same operations (=,!=,=~,!~)"; example of a label filter after a parser: "logfmt | duration > 1m and bytes_consumed > 20MB". Label names may contain ASCII letters, so `Message` is kept as is. stage-2 json-logs.txt lines carry no Timestamp field.
docker-compose.yml @ stage-3 defines separate services api (line 149), rabbitmq (268), notifications (308) and payments (359), each its own container.

Author-marked opinion that follows from verified claims 5-7 and 14 (request line and exception line share no request-identifying value; overlapping requests interleave). No version-dependent behaviour.

Grafana v12.4 Explore: "Explore is your starting point for querying, analyzing, and aggregating data in Grafana." "You can quickly begin creating queries to start analyzing data without having to create a dashboard". Loki query editor: "select the corresponding Builder and Code tabs"; "In Code mode, you can write complex queries using a text editor". Provisioned data source @ stage-2: `- name: Loki`.

ASP.NET Core docs: "ASP.NET Core apps should be designed to process many requests simultaneously. Asynchronous APIs allow a small pool of threads to handle thousands of concurrent requests". Kestrel: "optimized to handle a large number of concurrent connections". Each request's two lines are written at different points (claim 4), so two overlapping requests' lines can interleave in the console stream Alloy ships to Loki.
